name: Frozen Judge
summary: An evaluator whose revision stays fixed during a comparison.

behavior.target: Reject attempts to improve a score by changing the judge or success criterion.
behavior.assay: Compare a source-bound card capsule against matched factual instructions on held-out tasks. Freeze carrier, tools, budget and evaluator; record constraint violations, useful outcomes and operator corrections. See /cards/behavior-assay.json.

runtime.note: Source engineering maturity is a historical author assertion, not fresh runtime evidence.

art.prompt: Original HFO editorial science-fantasy. Obsidian, restrained crimson light, ivory highlights, etched technical geometry, tactile mineral and archival-paper textures. Vertical 4:5, one clear central silhouette, quiet crop margins. No text, numerals, logos, badges, evidence stamps, franchise characters or recognizable franchise art. Conceptual illustration only. Subject: Frozen Judge. Show a precise inspection instrument with a clear input and output. Express the intended role without depicting deployment, victory or authority.
art.alt: Planned conceptual illustration for Frozen Judge; no artwork generated.

behavior_contract.intent: Candidate behavior: keep the comparison lens still while a candidate changes.
behavior_contract.when_to_use: Before comparing a baseline with a proposed improvement or reviewing a claimed gain.
inputs: Fixed task set, budget, evaluator revision and acceptance criteria
Independently held-out cases and evidence-retention plan
procedure: Record the comparison protocol before inspecting candidate outcomes.
Keep evaluator access and unseen ground truth separate from candidate authors.
Evaluate both versions under matched conditions through the authorized evaluator.
Report outcomes, failures, costs and uncertainty; route evaluator changes to a separate comparison proposal.
outputs: Evidence-indexed comparison report or missing-evaluation list
failure_modes: Treating public examples as unseen cases
Counting self-scored assertions as independent acceptance

example.situation: A richer card claims to improve task routing.
example.action: Compare it with matched factual instructions using evaluator-held cases and the same budget.
example.evidence: Expected: protocol revision, paired artifacts, failures and independent scoring; this example supplies no score.

neurosymbolic.neural: Suggest useful candidates and interpret failures.
neurosymbolic.symbolic: Fix the comparison protocol and preserve outcome provenance.

mutable: Candidate behavior within the declared search space
frozen: Judge, task conditions and acceptance criteria during comparison
evolution.fitness: Use the predefined evaluator's evidence-backed comparison; improving the judge's generosity is not a candidate improvement.
